question: I'm an IS sophomore (P-014) with a Data Science concentration and BA minor. I plan to take 36-200 (Reasoning with Data). Can this satisfy both an IS foundation requirement and a BA minor requirement simultaneously?

domain_contributions.programs: IS degree: 36-200 may appear as an IS foundation or DS concentration course. BA minor: statistics/data courses may appear in BA minor requirements
domain_contributions.courses: 36-200 (Reasoning with Data, 9 units) — introductory statistics course with broad applicability

key_facts: 36-200 is a statistics/data reasoning course applicable across multiple programs
IS degree typically requires a statistics/quantitative reasoning course — 36-200 is a common choice
BA minor may or may not include 36-200 as an accepted course — verify against official BA minor list
Double-counting policy: if 36-200 satisfies IS requirement, it may not also count toward BA minor
P-014 should verify Stellic to see how 36-200 is currently mapped
wrong_if_single_domain: Checking only IS requirements confirms 36-200 fits. Checking only BA minor requirements may also confirm it fits. Without combining both and applying double-counting policy, the conflict is missed.
common_mistake: Applying 36-200 to both IS and BA minor requirements, thereby reducing total courses needed — this likely violates the double-counting rule
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs, IS): 36-200 satisfies IS quantitative foundation
Step 2 (programs, BA minor): Does 36-200 appear in BA minor requirements? → verify
Step 3 (policies): Double-counting rule → one requirement only
Conclusion: P-014 must choose which program 36-200 is applied to; likely IS (where it is more central)
